newsitem.title: USA: $16 billion flowed into stock funds in September - ICI.
newsitem.headline: $16 billion flowed into stock funds in September - ICI.

text.p: The amount of cash invested in mutual funds edged lower in September but appeared to be leveling off at a slower rate, an industry group said Wednesday.
About $16 billion flowed into U.S. stock mutual funds in September, compared with $17.93 billion in August, according to the Investment Company Institute, a trade group for the nation's mutual funds.
Bond and income funds had inflows of about $1.5 billion for September, vs. $1.6 billion in August.

The stock fund total "is generally in line with that of recent months," John Rea, ICI chief economist, said in a statement. "Beginning in June, the monthly net flow to equity funds moderated to a pace well below that recorded during the first six months of the year.
Rea said the slowdown was partly seasonal, with flows boosted early in the year by retirement-related investments.
In January, about $28.93 billion flowed in stock funds, with levels staying above $20 billion for each month in the first half.
The flows then dipped to $14.48 billion in June, and $5.80 billion in July.
